question_text: The prophet Elijah's confrontation with the prophets of Baal on Mount Carmel demonstrated that:
option_a: God alone is worthy of worship and answers prayer
option_b: Baal was also a powerful god
explanation: When fire from heaven consumed Elijah's sacrifice despite being drenched with water, it proved that the Lord is the true God, not Baal.

question_text: The prophet Elisha's healing of Naaman the Syrian leper teaches that:
option_a: God's healing is available to Gentiles who obey in faith
explanation: Naaman, a Gentile commander, was healed after humbling himself to dip in the Jordan River, showing God's mercy extends beyond Israel.

question_text: The parable of the hidden treasure and the pearl of great price (Matthew 13) teaches that:
option_a: The kingdom of God is worth sacrificing everything to obtain
option_d: Only the rich can enter the kingdom
explanation: Both parables illustrate that discovering the kingdom of God is so valuable that a person will gladly give up everything they have to possess it.

question_text: The apostle Paul's teaching in Romans 8 that 'nothing can separate us from the love of God' emphasizes:
option_a: The security of believers in Christ
option_c: That salvation can be lost easily
option_d: That God loves only some people
explanation: Paul lists numerous potential threats but concludes that no created thing can separate believers from God's love in Christ Jesus, affirming eternal security.

question_text: The story of Ananias and Sapphira in Acts 5 demonstrates that:
option_a: Lying to the Holy Spirit has serious consequences
option_d: The early church did not practice giving
explanation: Ananias and Sapphira died after lying about their donation, showing that deceit and hypocrisy are serious offenses against God's holiness.

question_text: The selection of Matthias to replace Judas as an apostle (Acts 1) demonstrates the early church's practice of:
option_a: Seeking God's guidance through prayer and casting lots
option_c: Appointing apostles by the Roman government
explanation: The disciples prayed and cast lots to choose Matthias, showing their dependence on God's direction in leadership selection.

question_text: The apostle Peter's teaching that believers are a 'chosen race, a royal priesthood' (1 Peter 2) emphasizes:
option_a: The dignity and calling of all believers
option_d: That believers should rule over others
explanation: Peter applies Old Testament titles for Israel to all believers, affirming their special status and priestly role in representing God to the world.

question_text: The parable of the persistent widow (Luke 18) teaches about:
option_a: The importance of persistent prayer and trusting God's justice
option_b: The weakness of women in society
explanation: The widow's persistence moved the unjust judge to act; Jesus uses this to encourage believers to pray continually and trust God's timely justice.

question_text: The apostle Paul's teaching on the 'resurrection body' in 1 Corinthians 15 emphasizes that:
option_a: The resurrected body will be imperishable and glorious
explanation: Paul describes the resurrection body as imperishable, glorious, powerful, and spiritual, contrasting it with the perishable natural body.

question_text: The miracle of Jesus healing the man with the withered hand on the Sabbath (Matthew 12) demonstrates that:
option_a: Doing good and saving life takes precedence over Sabbath rules
option_b: Healing on the Sabbath is forbidden
explanation: Jesus healed on the Sabbath, teaching that mercy and necessity override strict legalistic interpretations of Sabbath rest.

question_text: The prophet Isaiah's prophecy of the suffering servant (Isaiah 53) is interpreted by Christians as referring to:
option_a: Jesus Christ's sacrificial death for sins
explanation: Christians see the suffering servant who dies for the sins of others as a prophecy of Jesus' crucifixion and atoning death.

question_text: The apostle Paul's teaching on 'freedom in Christ' (Galatians 5) warns against using freedom to:
option_a: Indulge the sinful nature
explanation: Paul warns that freedom in Christ is not a license to sin but an opportunity to love and serve others, led by the Spirit.

question_text: The healing of the woman with the issue of blood (Mark 5) demonstrates the power of:
option_a: Faith in Jesus, even among crowds
explanation: The woman's faith in touching Jesus' garment led to her healing, showing that personal faith matters regardless of circumstances.

question_text: The parable of the friend at midnight (Luke 11) teaches about:
option_a: Persistent prayer and God's willingness to give
explanation: Jesus uses the parable of a friend who eventually gives bread due to persistence to encourage persistent prayer and trust in God's generosity.

question_text: The apostle Paul's teaching on 'spiritual warfare' (Ephesians 6) emphasizes that the battle is against:
option_a: Spiritual forces of evil, not flesh and blood
explanation: Paul clarifies that the struggle is against spiritual powers and evil forces, requiring spiritual armor rather than physical weapons.

question_text: The prophet Jeremiah's purchase of a field during the Babylonian siege (Jeremiah 32) demonstrated:
option_a: Faith in God's promise of future restoration
explanation: Jeremiah bought land as a symbolic act showing confidence that God would restore Israel from exile and that property would again have value.

question_text: The miracle of Jesus raising Jairus's daughter (Mark 5) demonstrates that:
option_a: Jesus has power over death
explanation: Jesus raised the dead girl, showing his authority over death itself and foreshadowing his own resurrection.

question_text: The parable of the two debtors (Luke 7) illustrates that:
option_a: Those forgiven much love much
explanation: The woman who anointed Jesus' feet loved much because she had been forgiven much, contrasting with the Pharisee who showed little love.

question_text: The apostle Paul's teaching on 'the fullness of Christ' (Ephesians 1) emphasizes that:
option_a: Christ is head over all things for the church
option_b: Christ is only head of the universe
explanation: Paul declares that God placed all things under Christ's feet and gave him as head over the church, which is his body.

question_text: The prophet Jonah's preaching to Nineveh resulted in:
option_a: The city's repentance and God's mercy
explanation: The people of Nineveh repented at Jonah's warning, and God relented from destroying them, demonstrating his mercy to repentant sinners.

question_text: The healing of the deaf and mute man (Mark 7) is notable because Jesus:
option_a: Used physical touch and spoke a word
explanation: Jesus put his fingers in the man's ears, touched his tongue, and said 'Ephphatha' (Be opened), demonstrating personal care in healing.

question_text: The parable of the growing seed (Mark 4) illustrates that:
option_a: The kingdom of God grows mysteriously beyond human control
explanation: The seed grows whether the farmer sleeps or wakes, showing that God's kingdom grows through divine power, not human effort alone.

question_text: The apostle Paul's teaching on 'the new covenant' (2 Corinthians 3) emphasizes that it is a covenant of:
option_a: The Spirit, not the letter
explanation: Paul contrasts the old covenant (written on stone, leading to death) with the new covenant (written on hearts by the Spirit, bringing life).

question_text: The prophet Ezekiel's call to be a 'watchman' for Israel (Ezekiel 33) emphasized his responsibility to:
option_a: Warn the wicked to turn from their ways
explanation: Ezekiel was to warn the people of coming judgment, with accountability for failing to sound the warning, emphasizing prophetic responsibility.

question_text: The healing of the ten lepers (Luke 17) is notable because only one:
option_a: Returned to give thanks
explanation: Only the Samaritan leper returned to thank Jesus, highlighting the importance of gratitude and faith.

question_text: The parable of the barren fig tree (Luke 13) teaches about:
option_a: God's patience and the opportunity for repentance
explanation: The owner gave the fig tree one more year to produce fruit, illustrating God's patience and mercy before judgment falls.

question_text: The apostle Paul's teaching on 'the mind of Christ' (Philippians 2) calls believers to:
option_a: Humility and putting others' interests first
explanation: Paul points to Christ's humility in emptying himself and becoming obedient to death, urging believers to adopt the same servant attitude.

question_text: The prophet Malachi's prophecy about Elijah coming before the great day of the Lord is interpreted in the New Testament as referring to:
option_a: John the Baptist
explanation: Jesus identified John the Baptist as the Elijah who was to come, preparing the way for the Messiah.

question_text: The miracle of Jesus feeding the 4,000 (Matthew 15) is significant because it:
option_a: Shows Jesus' compassion for Gentiles
option_b: Was a miracle for Jews only
explanation: The feeding of 4,000 occurred in a Gentile region (Decapolis), showing Jesus' compassion for non-Jews as well.

question_text: The parable of the wheat and the tares (Matthew 13) teaches that:
option_a: Good and evil will coexist until the final judgment
option_b: Believers should immediately remove sinners from the church
explanation: The wheat and tares grow together until harvest, representing believers and unbelievers coexisting until God's final judgment separates them.

question_text: The apostle Paul's teaching on 'the day of the Lord' (1 Thessalonians 5) emphasizes that it will come:
option_a: Like a thief in the night
explanation: Paul warns that the day of the Lord will come unexpectedly, like a thief, calling believers to be alert and sober.

question_text: The prophet Haggai's message encouraged the returned exiles to:
option_a: Rebuild the temple
explanation: Haggai challenged the people to prioritize rebuilding God's temple rather than their own homes, promising blessing for obedience.

question_text: The healing of the royal official's son (John 4) is notable because Jesus healed:
option_a: From a distance, without physical contact
explanation: Jesus healed the official's son from a distance when the father believed his word, demonstrating his power beyond physical presence.

question_text: The parable of the dragnet (Matthew 13) illustrates that:
option_a: Final judgment will separate the righteous from the wicked
option_b: Fishing is a metaphor for evangelism only
explanation: The dragnet gathers all kinds of fish, which are then sorted, representing the final separation of good from evil at the end of the age.

question_text: The apostle Paul's teaching on 'the mystery of godliness' (1 Timothy 3) refers to:
option_a: Christ's incarnation, vindication, and exaltation
explanation: Paul summarizes the faith as Christ revealed in the flesh, vindicated by the Spirit, preached to the nations, and exalted in glory.

question_text: The prophet Zechariah's vision of the four chariots symbolized God's:
option_a: Judgment and protection over the nations
explanation: The chariots represent God's spirits going throughout the earth to execute judgment and protection.

question_text: The miracle of Jesus healing the man born blind (John 9) resulted in:
option_a: His confession of faith in Jesus
explanation: After being healed, the man confessed faith in Jesus despite opposition from the Pharisees, demonstrating spiritual as well as physical sight.

question_text: The parable of the unmerciful servant (Matthew 18) teaches that:
option_a: Forgiven people must forgive others
explanation: The servant who was forgiven a huge debt refused to forgive a small debt, illustrating that those who receive God's forgiveness must extend it to others.

question_text: The apostle Paul's teaching on 'the body of Christ' (1 Corinthians 12) emphasizes:
option_a: Unity and diversity within the church
explanation: Paul uses the human body as a metaphor for the church, showing that different gifts work together in unity for the common good.

question_text: The prophet Zephaniah's message emphasized the coming 'day of the Lord' as a time of:
option_a: Judgment on Judah and the nations
explanation: Zephaniah warned of God's impending judgment on Judah for idolatry and on surrounding nations, but also promised future restoration.

question_text: The healing of the paralytic at the pool of Bethesda (John 5) is notable because:
option_a: Jesus healed on the Sabbath
explanation: Jesus healed on the Sabbath, leading to controversy with Jewish leaders who accused him of breaking the Sabbath law.

question_text: The parable of the faithful and wise servant (Matthew 24) teaches about:
option_a: Being ready for the Master's return
option_b: The value of sleeping on the job
explanation: The faithful servant continues doing his master's work until his return, while the wicked servant abuses others and is punished.

question_text: The apostle Paul's teaching on 'justification by faith' in Romans 3-4 is based on the example of:
option_a: Abraham, who believed God
explanation: Paul argues that Abraham was justified by faith before circumcision and the law, making him the father of all who believe.

question_text: The prophet Obadiah's prophecy focused on judgment against:
option_a: Edom
explanation: Obadiah prophesies against Edom for rejoicing over Jerusalem's destruction and mistreating God's people.

question_text: The miracle of Jesus walking on water (Matthew 14) demonstrated his power over:
option_a: Natural forces
explanation: Jesus walking on the stormy sea showed his authority over creation and natural forces, leading the disciples to worship him as Son of God.

question_text: The parable of the laborers in the vineyard (Matthew 20) teaches about:
option_a: God's generosity and grace regardless of when people come to faith
option_b: The importance of working longer hours
explanation: All workers received the same wage regardless of hours worked, illustrating that God's grace and salvation are gifts, not earned rewards.

question_text: The apostle Paul's teaching on 'the fruit of the Spirit' (Galatians 5) includes:
option_a: Love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faithfulness, gentleness, self-control
explanation: Paul lists nine virtues produced by the Holy Spirit in believers' lives, contrasting them with the works of the flesh.

question_text: The prophet Joel's prophecy about pouring out the Spirit was fulfilled at:
option_a: Pentecost
explanation: Peter quoted Joel's prophecy at Pentecost, when the Holy Spirit was poured out on all believers.

question_text: The healing of the demon-possessed boy (Mark 9) teaches about:
option_a: The power of faith and prayer
explanation: When the disciples couldn't heal, Jesus cast out the demon, saying 'Everything is possible for one who believes.'

question_text: The parable of the great banquet (Luke 14) illustrates that:
option_a: The invitation to God's kingdom is extended to all
explanation: When invited guests refused, the master invited the poor, crippled, blind, and lame, showing God's kingdom open to all who accept.

question_text: The apostle Paul's teaching on 'the armor of God' (Ephesians 6) includes the:
option_a: Belt of truth, breastplate of righteousness, shield of faith
option_b: Sword of knowledge, helmet of intelligence
option_c: Armor of power, shield of might
option_d: Weapons of force, armor of steel
explanation: Paul lists spiritual armor: truth, righteousness, readiness, faith, salvation, God's word, and prayer for spiritual battle.
